extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, AMS members, graduate students, and librarians ordering mathematical books
extracted.subtask_description: A society-news/Notices page listing new AMS book publications (with target readership/prerequisites and ordering codes), society statistics on women mathematicians, and officers/committee membership and procedural rules. Useful for readers tracking publications, committee composition, and reporting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of names by gender/foreignness
rubrics_metrics.description: Since name identification was used, the information for some categories necessitated the use of four classifications: Male: names that were obviously male; Female: names that were obviously female; Unknown: names that could not be identified as clearly male or female (e.g., only initials given); and Foreign: foreign names that could not be identified as clearly male or female.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This four-part classification system was used to categorize individuals when compiling statistics on the relative numbers of men versus women in specified AMS categories; it acknowledges limitations when only initials or unfamiliar/foreign names are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories for annual reporting on women
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council approved a motion to regularly assemble and report information on the relative numbers of men versus women in at least the following categories: membership in the AMS; invited hour addresses at AMS meetings; speakers at special sessions at AMS meetings; and members of editorial boards of AMS journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional information on the number of Ph.D.'s granted to women is to be collected using the AMS-MAA Annual Survey. Updated reports will appear annually in the Notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology: determine sex based on name identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Information would be gathered by determining the sex of the individuals in the above categories based on name identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because this method relies on perceived gender from names, the classification can produce 'Unknown' or 'Foreign' categories when names are ambiguous or not readily classifiable; users should note this limitation when interpreting the statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated reports will appear annually in the Notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statistics described (e.g., on membership, invited addresses, editorial boards, Ph.D. production) are intended to be compiled and published on a yearly basis to track trends over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms expiration rule for officers and committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms of members expire on January 31 following the year given unless otherwise specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural rule governs the listed officers and committee members and clarifies the effective end date of the terms shown in the listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Secretary voting membership rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one Associate Secretary at a time is a voting member of the Council, namely the cognizant Associate Secretary for the scientific sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specifies which Associate Secretary holds voting privileges on the Council when more than one Associate Secretary position exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex officio membership rule for certain committees
rubrics_metrics.description: All members of this committee serve ex officio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several committee entries explicitly state that 'all members of this committee serve ex officio,' indicating that membership is by virtue of holding another office rather than by separate appointment; applies to multiple named committees in the listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monograph suitability as an advanced graduate textbook
rubrics_metrics.description: This monograph provides a careful and accessible exposition of functional analytic methods in stochastic analysis... The book would be suitable as a textbook in a one-year, advanced graduate course on functional analysis and partial differential equations, with emphasis on their strong interrelations with probability theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers' descriptive remarks are treated as evaluative guidance about appropriate course placement and intended instructional use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader prerequisites for specific monographs
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Ramanujan continued fractions volume: 'The only required background is some knowledge of continued fractions and a course in complex analysis.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher notes on required background identify the minimal mathematical preparation expected of the target reader for the book; useful for librarians, instructors, and potential readers evaluating suitability.
